GRIM-test with hypothetical group sizes

Source: R/grim-map-total-n.R
grim_map_total_n.Rd

Some studies report group means but only the total sample size, not the group sizes. For two groups, grim_map_total_n() tests hypothetical splits of the total: it starts from an even split, moves one participant at a time from one group to the other, and GRIM-tests both means against both group sizes, in both pairings.

Call audit() on the output for summary statistics.

Usage

grim_map_total_n(
  data,
  digits_x,
  x1 = NULL,
  x2 = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  ...,
  items_averaged,
  data_type,
  x_meaning = c("mean", "percentage"),
  rounding = "up_or_down",
  threshold = 5,
  symmetric = FALSE,
  show_rec = FALSE,
  dispersion = 0:5,
  n_min = 1L,
  n_max = NULL,
  constant = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with numeric columns x1, x2, and n: the two group means (or percentages) and the total sample size. Which mean is x1 does not matter, since both pairings with the group sizes are tested.

digits_x

Integer. The number of decimal places in x1 and x2, including trailing zeros. There is no default, since a numeric value does not keep them (1.40 is 1.4). Either a single number for both groups, or two numbers, one for x1 and one for x2, which apply to every row of data. If left out, it is taken from a digits_x column of data, with one number per row for both groups. If the decimal places differ both by group and by row, call the function on each set of rows separately and audit() each output.

x1, x2, n

Optionally, the names of the columns in data that contain these values, if they differ from the defaults.

...

These dots must be empty. Every argument after them must be named in full.

items_averaged

Integer. As in grim(): the number of items averaged into each score, not the number of scale points. Give it as an argument or as a column of data; there is no default. It is returned as a column.

data_type

String. As in grim(): "integer" or "continuous". Like items_averaged, give it as an argument or as a column of data; there is no default. It is returned as a column.

x_meaning

String. What the x values are: "mean" (the default) or "percentage". Percentages are divided by 100 and tested with two more decimal places. It applies to the whole call, so test a table that mixes means and percentages in parts, as in the examples of grim_map(). The parts record different settings, so they can't be combined with dplyr::bind_rows(). See Defaults in grim().

rounding, threshold, symmetric

Passed on to grim(), whose section Defaults explains the defaults.

show_rec

Logical. If TRUE, the reconstructed numbers are returned as columns; see Reconstructed numbers in grim_map(). Default is FALSE.

dispersion

Numeric. Steps up and down from half the total n. Default is 0:5, i.e., the even split and five steps away from it.

n_min

Numeric. Minimal group size. Default is 1.

n_max

Numeric. Maximal group size. Default is NULL, i.e., no maximum.

constant

Optionally, values that belong to the two groups, such as their labels: a length-2 vector for the groups of x1 and x2, or a list of such vectors. Each becomes a column, as in disperse_total(), and its values stay with their groups in both directions. Default is NULL.

Value

A tibble with these columns:

  • x: the reported means, in pairs of rows.

  • n: the hypothetical group sizes, with n_change recording the steps from half the total.

  • both_consistent: whether both means of a pair are consistent with their hypothetical group sizes.

  • case: the row number in data.

  • dir: "forth" where x2 is paired with the larger group size, "back" where x1 is. The split of an even total into two equal groups is the same scenario either way, so it appears under "forth" only.

  • The other columns of grim_map() output, and the other columns of data.

Summaries with audit()

audit() on grim_map_total_n() output returns a tibble with one row per case and these columns:

  • x1, x2, and n: the reported values.

  • hits_total: the number of scenarios in which both groups are GRIM-consistent, summing hits_forth and hits_back.

  • hits_forth: the number of such scenarios with x2 paired with the larger group.

  • hits_back: the same with x1 paired with the larger group.

  • scenarios_total: the number of scenarios tested, each a split of n with one pairing of groups and statistics, leaving out those that could not be decided.

  • hit_rate: hits_total / scenarios_total, or NA if no scenario could be decided.

A count is NA if it depends on a scenario that could not be decided, or on rows removed from the output, as by filter().

Call audit() again on that summary to summarize these columns further.

References

Bauer, P. J., & Francis, G. (2021). Expression of Concern: Is It Light or Dark? Recalling Moral Behavior Changes Perception of Brightness. Psychological Science, 32(12), 2042–2043. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/09567976211058727

Brown, N. J. L., & Heathers, J. A. J. (2017). The GRIM Test: A Simple Technique Detects Numerous Anomalies in the Reporting of Results in Psychology. Social Psychological and Personality Science, 8(4), 363–369. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1948550616673876

See also

function_map_total_n(), which created this function from grim_map().

Examples

df <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x1,  ~x2,  ~n,
  3.43, 5.28, 90,
  2.97, 4.42, 103
)

grim_map_total_n(df, digits_x = 2, items_averaged = 1, data_type = "integer")
#> # A tibble: 46 × 11
#> # GRIM: default settings
#>        x     n n_change items_averaged data_type digits_x consistency
#>    <dbl> <int>    <int>          <int> <chr>        <int> <lgl>      
#>  1  3.43    45        0              1 integer          2 FALSE      
#>  2  5.28    45        0              1 integer          2 FALSE      
#>  3  3.43    44       -1              1 integer          2 TRUE       
#>  4  5.28    46        1              1 integer          2 TRUE       
#>  5  3.43    43       -2              1 integer          2 FALSE      
#>  6  5.28    47        2              1 integer          2 TRUE       
#>  7  3.43    42       -3              1 integer          2 TRUE       
#>  8  5.28    48        3              1 integer          2 FALSE      
#>  9  3.43    41       -4              1 integer          2 FALSE      
#> 10  5.28    49        4              1 integer          2 FALSE      
#> # ℹ 36 more rows
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: both_consistent <lgl>, exp_incon <dbl>, case <int>,
#> #   dir <fct>

# `hits_total` counts the splits in which both means are consistent:
df |>
  grim_map_total_n(digits_x = 2, items_averaged = 1, data_type = "integer") |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>      x1    x2     n hits_total hits_forth hits_back scenarios_total hit_rate
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <int>      <int>      <int>     <int>           <int>    <dbl>
#> 1  3.43  5.28    90          3          2         1              11    0.273
#> 2  2.97  4.42   103          0          0         0              12    0    

# More steps away from the even split tend to find more hits:
df |>
  grim_map_total_n(
    digits_x = 2,
    items_averaged = 1,
    data_type = "integer",
    dispersion = 0:10
  ) |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>      x1    x2     n hits_total hits_forth hits_back scenarios_total hit_rate
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <int>      <int>      <int>     <int>           <int>    <dbl>
#> 1  3.43  5.28    90          6          3         3              21   0.286 
#> 2  2.97  4.42   103          2          0         2              22   0.0909
